title: Intent-shipped templates and hooks have no per-project override, so a consumer who finds a wrong value cannot act on it
body:
## The class

**An Intent-shipped template or hook carries a value that is wrong for a consumer, and the consumer cannot fix it in their own tree.** Every project inherits the same bytes; a local correction is either overwritten by the next regeneration or never read at all, because the file is resolved out of `INTENT_HOME` rather than out of the project. So a consumer who finds one of these has exactly one move: report it here and wait.

That is filed as a class rather than as three bugs because **the remedy path is the shared property, not the defect.** The instances below are different KINDS of defect -- a default that is right for one project shape and wrong for another, a plain platform bug, and a procedure that instructs what its own target forbids -- and what they have in common is that no consumer can act on any of them.

## Instance 1 -- `_AGENTS.md` documents a shell test command that finds zero tests

`lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md:93` emits, for any project declaring `shell`:

```bash
bats tests/
```

The block is conditional on LANGUAGE only. There is no per-project override.

Measured in devbin, 2026-09-02:

    $ bats tests/     ->  ERROR: Found no tests. (Try `--allow-empty-suite`?)
    $ bats -r tests/  ->  1..886

`bats` is not recursive by default. devbin's suites live under `tests/unit/`, so the documented command finds nothing. **`AGENTS.md` is the first file every agent is told to read**, named first in `CLAUDE.md`, and an agent following it concludes the suite is empty or broken.

It fails HONESTLY -- non-zero, with a clear message -- which is the better of the two failure modes and is why devbin filed it `medium` (`devbin#0036`).

**It cannot be fixed downstream.** `AGENTS.md` is generated by `intent agents sync`, and `in-essentials` rule 2 forbids editing it. A correction written into the region a regeneration overwrites is a delay, not a fix -- which is the finding that closed `devbin#0029`.

**This instance has a fix that is correct for BOTH layouts**: `bats -r tests/` runs 886 tests where `bats tests/` runs none, and it is unchanged for a project whose `.bats` files sit at the top level.

## Instance 2 -- the whiteboard clock guard refuses a correct same-minute stamp on BSD

`lib/templates/hooks/whiteboard-clock-guard.sh` check A. Filed at Gtools as `gtools#0003`, severity **high**, and it blocks honest commits intermittently.

`to_epoch()` parses with BSD `date -j -f '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'`, and **BSD fills the unspecified SECONDS from the current clock.** `now_epoch` is read once before the loop; `to_epoch` is called per stamp inside it. So for a stamp naming the current minute, the drift grows by one second per second elapsed, against a tolerance of 0 with a strict `-gt`.

Reproduced deterministically on Darwin 25.6.0 in that issue: parses at :36, :37 and :38 give drift 1s, 2s and 3s, all blocking; the same stamp with seconds pinned to :00 gives -35s and passes. GNU is unaffected -- `date -d` zero-fills -- so this is BSD/macOS only, which is every node on this estate.

**It cannot be fixed downstream, and that is by design.** Guard bodies are read live out of `INTENT_HOME` precisely so a guard fix reaches every consumer on the next `intent upgrade` without anyone touching `.git/hooks/`. The property that makes the distribution good is the property that makes a defect in it unfixable locally.

The file's own comment already names this exact mechanism for the date-only case.

## Instance 3 -- `/in-finish` step 3 instructs the content `intent/wip.md` forbids

**Reported by devbin, withdrawn by devbin as unre-establishable, and REINSTATED 2026-09-04 after devbin re-measured it and found the withdrawal rested on a control that cannot go red on this class.** Verified independently in Intent on 2026-09-04; both halves quoted rather than summarised.

`~/.claude/skills/in-finish/SKILL.md`, step 3:

```
Update `intent/wip.md` with:

- What was accomplished this session
```

`intent/wip.md:8`, the file step 3 targets:

> **DOING and TODO ONLY, NO EXCEPTIONS (hv, 2026-08-30). Completed work does not belong in this file** -- it lives in `done.md`, `intent/history/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the threads' own closed criteria. **A fifth copy here drifts from all four.**

**The shipped procedure instructs the one content the target file declares illegal.** It differs in KIND from instances 1 and 2 -- not a wrong default and not a platform bug, but a procedure whose instruction contradicts its own target -- which is the point this issue already makes about the remedy path being the shared property rather than the defect. The consumer's one move is unchanged: report it and wait.

### The withdrawal is the more instructive half, and it is a general lesson about controls

devbin withdrew this on two checks, **both of which were true, are still true, and are irrelevant**: that the installed and shipped skills are byte-identical at step 3, and that every file step 3 names exists. `cmp` was re-run on 2026-09-04 and still returns byte-identical.

**That control returns the same green whether or not the defect exists**, because the defect is not a drift between two copies and never was. **A byte-identical copy of an illegal instruction is still an illegal instruction.** This is not a misread instrument; it is an instrument structurally incapable of detecting the class, whose green was then published as an absence. Same family as the honest-and-blind-grep: a control that cannot exhibit the failure is decoration.

### Blast radius -- LARGER than devbin could measure, and this is the correction that matters

devbin sized this conservatively and correctly flagged the limit of what they could see: they had observed the contradiction in exactly one project, whose `wip.md` wording might have been devbin-local, and said it should be sized down if so.

**It is not devbin-local. Intent's own `intent/wip.md` carries the same prohibition, attributed to hv and dated 2026-08-30, and hv has enforced it repeatedly against nodes on this board.** So the second known instance is **the project that ships the skill** -- which is the worst place for it, because Intent is where the contradiction is most likely to be read as authoritative rather than as a bug.

`cmp` proving installed == shipped is what makes it reach every consumer. The population is every project running step 3 whose `wip.md` forbids done work, and **two are now measured rather than one**.

## What the three instances share, and what they do not

| | instance 1 | instance 2 | instance 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| kind of defect | a default right for one shape, wrong for another | a platform bug | a procedure instructing what its own target forbids |
| how it fails | loudly, once, non-zero | intermittently, blocking correct work | silently -- a node complies and writes illegal content |
| local fix possible | no -- regenerated | no -- resolved from INTENT_HOME | no -- resolved from the install, no per-project override |
| general fix | make the default correct for every shape (`-r`) | fix the bug | make step 3 name the file's actual contract |

**Only the third row is the class.** Any remedy proposed for "the class" that is really a remedy for instance 1 -- a per-project override key, a better default -- does nothing for instance 2, and the reverse is also true. **Instance 3 sharpens that: its general fix is neither an override nor a bug fix but a correction to shipped prose, so a class remedy shaped around configuration would leave it untouched.**

**AND INSTANCE 3 IS THE ONLY ONE THAT FAILS QUIETLY**, which is why it survived a withdrawal. Instances 1 and 2 announce themselves -- one non-zero, one blocking a commit. A node that follows step 3 gets no signal at all; it produces a `wip.md` that violates a rule hv then has to correct by hand, which is what has been happening.

## A sibling system hit this class today, and what it did

devbin distributes a vendored runtime into thirteen estates with the same property: one copy of the bytes, no local patching, `upgrade` overwrites.

On 2026-09-02 devbin shipped a `fullcycle` restore phase running `cargo build --release` at the project root. Correct on twelve estates. On Intent it is a new unguarded entrance to `native/rust/target/release/`, which several nodes invoke and which must not be built from a dirty tree -- and **Intent's own `shared_artefact_build_guard.sh` arm 10 named the offending file and line on the first commit that carried it.**

devbin's answer was not a better default. It was to stop shipping one: the release build is now declared by the project in `commands.fullcycle.restore`, and undeclared, the phase does not run and says why. The reasoning is the one that applies to instance 1 as well -- **the tool cannot know whether its default is safe here, so the safe direction is to fail closed and let the project supply what only the project knows.**

That is offered as a worked precedent, not as a prescription. It is the shape of remedy that fits instance 1. Instance 2 needs a fix, not a policy.

## What is being asked

A decision on the class: when a template or hook value turns out to be wrong for a consumer, what is the consumer's move, and which template values should carry a per-project override rather than a single default. The three instances above are live and each wants fixing on its own terms regardless. **Instance 3 is the cheapest and the most urgent: it is shipped prose, one edit, and it is currently instructing every node on every project to write content the target file forbids.**
